summary: El Salvador waives visas for a broad list including the US, UK, EU, Canada, Australia, Japan and most of the Americas — many visitors just pay USD 12 for a tourist card on arrival and share a single 90-day stay across the CA-4 zone (El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua). Remaining nationalities need a consular visa.

currencyLimits.text: Cash or negotiable instruments of USD 10,000 or more must be declared on arrival and departure.

payments.text: The US dollar has been El Salvador's currency since 2001, so there is nothing to exchange for most visitors. Cards are fine in San Salvador's malls, hotels and chain restaurants; carry small bills for pupuserías, buses and beach towns. Bitcoin lost its legal-tender status in January 2025. Some businesses still take it voluntarily, but none are obliged to.

safety.text: El Salvador's security situation has improved dramatically since 2022 — homicide rates are now among the lowest in the Americas and travel advisories have been relaxed accordingly. The state-of-exception security regime remains in force: carry ID, cooperate at checkpoints, and steer clear of anything that could be read as gang imagery, including certain tattoos.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — El Salvador travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: The dry season from November to April is best for volcano hikes, the Ruta de las Flores and the beaches; surfers get the most consistent Pacific swell from about March to October.

idp.text: El Salvador is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: El Salvador is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for El Salvador yet.

tips.text: El Salvador shares one 90-day stay with Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua (the CA-4). Crossing between the four does not reset your clock. Plan an extension, or a trip outside the zone (Costa Rica, Mexico or Belize), before day 90.
Have USD 12 ready for the tourist card on arrival. Cards usually work at the airport, but cash is the safe bet at land borders.
Bitcoin is no longer legal tender. The law was rolled back in January 2025 as part of El Salvador's IMF agreement. Chivo wallet infrastructure is being wound down, so carry ordinary dollars.

The state of exception in force since 2022 gives police broad detention powers. Carry your passport (or a copy), be patient at checkpoints, and avoid clothing or tattoos that could be mistaken for gang symbols.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for El Salvador?
faq.answer: Most visitors do not: the US, UK, EU, Canada, Australia, Japan and nearly all of the Americas are visa-exempt for 90 days. Many of these nationalities pay USD 12 for a tourist card on arrival. Nationalities outside the exemption list need a consular visa, or can generally enter with the tourist card if they hold a valid US visa.

faq.question: What is the USD 12 tourist card?
faq.answer: A small entry fee-and-form collected on arrival from visa-exempt nationalities that are not fee-exempt — US and Canadian passport holders pay it, while Central American neighbors and several treaty countries do not. It covers your whole 90-day CA-4 stay; pay in cash at land borders.

faq.question: Does time in Guatemala or Honduras count against my El Salvador stay?
faq.answer: Yes. El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua form the CA-4 zone with a single shared 90-day stay. Border hops within the zone do not restart it. You can apply for one extension at Migración, or leave the zone entirely (e.g. To Costa Rica, Belize or Mexico) before re-entering.

faq.question: Do I need Bitcoin to pay for things in El Salvador?
faq.answer: No. Bitcoin's legal-tender status was repealed in January 2025, so no business is required to accept it. A few tourist spots (notably El Zonte's "Bitcoin Beach") still do by choice. The everyday currency is the US dollar.

faq.question: Is El Salvador safe to visit now?
faq.answer: Far safer than its old reputation: since the 2022 crackdown, homicide rates have fallen to among the lowest in the Western Hemisphere and tourism has surged. Petty theft still exists, and the ongoing state of exception means you should always carry ID and comply at police checkpoints.
